title: Neural Representation Interface document, v0.1
description: A typed, executable description of what a network computes. Every claim is a predicate an executor checks against the network; status is written by the executor, never by the author.

blinded.description: true if the author had no access to training code, task description or ground truth

variables.description: Computational variables. `ftype` is the ANLU-style functional type of the VARIABLE (what role it plays in the computation), independent of whether the network was trained with type embeddings.

binding.description: Python lambda over the input token list t, returning an int: how to compute the variable's ground value from the input

output_fn.description: Python lambda over dict v of variable values, returning the predicted output class

kind.description: behavior: model output == output_fn on >= threshold. linear_rep: a CAUSAL claim, tested by interchange intervention (swap the rank-r class-mean subspace of the variable between two inputs; output must follow output_fn with the variable taken from the source). Linear decodability alone does NOT pass it. necessity: mean-ablating that subspace drops behavior accuracy to <= threshold. edit: a weight program; success in scope, preservation out of scope, rank and relative norm reported.

scope.description: lambda v: bool, which inputs the edit is meant to change

edit_fn.description: lambda v: int, desired output after the edit

predicate.description: [op, threshold] for scalar claims; {metric: [op, threshold]} for edit claims

status.description: written by the executor: verified | refuted | error: ...
